# Adjudication Task — Chapter 447

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃447화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|촤아아아.
  6|
  7|빠르게 물살을 가르며 나아가는 쾌조선에는 침묵만이 감돌았다.
  8|
  9|수룡채의 수적들은 입을 꾹 다문 채 기계처럼 노를 저었고, 무송은 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴로 전방을 주시할 뿐이었다.
 10|
 11|‘분위기 한번 끝내주네.’
 12|
 13|나는 내심 혀를 차며 주위를 둘러보았다.
 14|
 15|현재 동정채로 향하는 쾌조선은 총 네 척.
 16|
 17|하지만 선상의 분위기는 호북으로 향하던 때와는 천양지차다.
 18|
 19|전에는 찾아볼 수 없었던 새로운 얼굴들이 바로 그 원인이었다.
 20|
 21|‘제갈세가. 그리고 무당파.’
 22|
 23|호북성을 양분하는 두 명문 대파의 제자들이 네 척의 쾌조선을 가득 채웠다.
 24|
 25|혹시 모를 유혈 사태를 대비하여 가려 뽑은 정예라는 걸 한눈에 알 수 있을 만큼, 한 사람 한 사람이 뛰어난 무인들이다.
 26|
 27|그리고 그들의 중심에는 두 사람이 있었다.
 28|
 29|“오늘따라 유독 바람이 강한 것 같구려, 제갈가주.”
 30|
 31|노도사의 말에 제갈풍이 태평한 목소리로 대답했다.
 32|
 33|“염려하지 않으셔도 됩니다. 오늘 같은 바람이 분다면 오히려 일이 더욱 수월해질 테니까요.”
 34|
 35|“어째서 그렇소? 이보다 약한 바람에도 이미 수십 척의 배가 수몰한 것으로 알고 있소만.”
 36|
 37|“수부들의 실력도 실력이지만, 장강수로맹의 상징이라 할 수 있는 쾌조선은 여타의 배와는 질적으로 다릅니다. 강풍에 휩쓸리기보다 힘을 받고 더욱 힘차게 나아갈 수 있지요.”
 38|
 39|“빈도 역시 쾌조선에 관한 풍월을 들은 적이 있긴 하오만…… 견문이 좁은 탓에 자세히는 모르겠구려. 일평생 무림에 몸담은 것이 허송세월처럼 느껴질 정도요.”
 40|
 41|“진인께서는 무당파 본산에만 머무르셨으니 모르실 만도 하지요. 그런데…… 지난번 말씀하셨던 그 일은 어떻게 되었는지 여쭤봐도 되겠습니까?”
 42|
 43|“장문인께서 직접 본 산의 제자들과 함께 힘쓰고 계시는 중이오. 그 대신 빈둥거리며 양곡만 축내는 빈도를 이리 보내신 것이고.”
 44|
 45|“양곡만 축내다니요. 이 후배는 현공진인(玄空眞人)께서 오시니 천군만마를 얻은 듯합니다.”
 46|
 47|제갈풍의 말은 예의상 하는 것이 아니었다. 사실이 그랬다.
 48|
 49|현공진인.
 50|
 51|그것이 누덕누덕 기운 도복과 낡은 송문고검(松紋古劍) 한 자루를 허리춤에 찬 노도사의 도호였다.
 52|
 53|그리고 그가 무당파 내에서 차지하는 위치나 무림의 배분은 결코 제갈풍에 뒤떨어지지 않았다.
 54|
 55|아니, 오히려 어깨를 나란히 하거나 그 이상이라고도 할 수 있었다.
 56|
 57|아직 환갑도 되지 않은 제갈풍과 달리, 현공진인은 정마대전 당시에도 혁혁한 전공을 올린 전대의 고수이자 현 무당파 장문인의 사제니까.
 58|
 59|‘게다가 무당파가 자랑하는 초절정 고수이기도 하고.’
 60|
 61|무당파 최고의 절기, 태극혜검(太極慧劍)의 극의에 다다랐다고 알려진 검객이 바로 현공진인이었다.
 62|
 63|제갈세가의 가주인 제갈풍이 다른 이들 앞에서도 말을 높이는 것 역시 그에 대한 존중의 표시였다.
 64|
 65|아, 물론 한 사람은 이 모든 것에서 예외다.
 66|
 67|“많이 컸네, 저놈.”
 68|
 69|무림의 달마대사 고인물, 적천강의 말에 어이가 없어진 내가 중얼거렸다.
 70|
 71|“그러게요. 얼마나 많이 컸는지 수염이 허옇네.”
 72|
 73|“마지막으로 봤을 때 저놈 나이가 이립이었던가. 허, 참. 시간 한번 빠르다. 솜털 보송보송하던 어린 녀석들이 죄다 일파의 장문인이고 장로라니.”
 74|
 75|“……솜털 보송보송이요? 이립이면 고추 털 수북 아닙니까?”
 76|
 77|적천강이 쌍심지 켠 눈으로 나를 바라보았다.
 78|
 79|“계속 말꼬리를 잡는 걸 보아하니, 아래 털이 죄다 뽑히고 싶은 모양이로구나.”
 80|
 81|“아니, 무슨 그런 말씀을 하세요.”
 82|
 83|쾌조선 갑판 위에서 화왕질리언 왁싱을 당할 마음은 눈곱만큼도 없다.
 84|
 85|빛의 속도로 손을 내저은 내가 슬쩍 적천강을 곁눈질하며 물었다.
 86|
 87|“이렇게 된 김에 여쭤보는 건데, 춘추가 정확히 얼마나 되시는 겁니까?”
 88|
 89|“춘추?”
 90|
 91|평소에도 늙었다는 소리를 죽여 달라는 것과 동의어로 받아들이는 적천강이다. 나는 떨떠름하게 단어를 고쳤다.
 92|
 93|“……그럼, 연세?”
 94|
 95|“연세?”
 96|
 97|아니, 백 세가 넘었으면서 도대체 여기서 뭘 더 원하는 거야.
 98|
 99|나는 어이없음을 한껏 담아 물었다.
100|
101|“천강이, 몇 살?”
102|
103|빡!
104|
105|그래, 이럴 줄 알았다.
106|
107|번개처럼 내 뒤통수를 후려친 적천강이 심드렁한 어조로 대답했다.
108|
109|“일백을 넘긴 후로 안 세 봤다.”
110|
111|“그러니까 마지막으로 나이를 셌던 게 몇 년 전인데요?”
112|
113|“오천 년 전. 됐느냐?”
114|
115|근처 뱃머리에 대롱대롱 매달려 있던 청풍이 입을 딱 벌렸다.
116|
117|“와아, 오천 살!”
118|
119|“……저놈은 의심이란 걸 할 줄 모르냐?”
120|
121|“……원래 그런 놈입니다. 그나저나 상상을 초월할 정도로 동안이셨네요.”
122|
123|적천강이 나를 지그시 노려보았다.
124|
125|“더 자세히 알고 싶으냐?”
126|
127|“당연히, 아니죠.”
128|
129|솔직히 알고 싶긴 한데, 표정을 보니 알아서는 안 될 것 같다.
130|
131|평소 나이에 민감한 건 둘째 치고, 어느 때보다 거친 물살과 바람을 타고 빠르게 나아가는 쾌조선에 타고 있다는 현실이 그에게 엄청난 스트레스로 다가온 모양이었다.
132|
133|“도대체 이 염병할 나무 쪼가리는 언제쯤 멈추는 게냐?”
134|
135|바로 그때.
136|
137|적천강의 투덜거림을 듣기라도 한 것처럼 염병할 나무 쪼가리가 더욱 속력을 높였다.
138|
139|콰아아아!
140|
141|물줄기가 높이 솟구치며 안정적이던 선체가 좌우로 흔들렸다.
142|
143|갑작스러운 거친 움직임에 청풍이 어린이날 놀이공원에 온 아이처럼 환호를 질렀다.
144|
145|아직까지도 장강 찍먹 사건의 후유증을 벗어나지 못한 혁무진과 궁기방은 찢어지는 비명을 내질렀고, 평온하게 홀로 중심을 잡고 있던 문경은 사람들의 시선을 의식하여 눈치껏 난간을 붙잡았다.
146|
147|그리고 적천강은…….
148|
149|“으허, 으허어어어어!”
150|
151|화왕(火王)이라는 별호가 무색할 만한 소리를 내며 혼비백산하는 중이다.
152|
153|세상에, 눈 부릅뜬 거 봐. 강남 성형외과 쌍꺼풀 수술 성공 사례로 지하철 전면 광고 실어도 되겠다.
154|
155|나는 얼굴로 쏟아지는 물을 피하며 무송을 향해 외쳤다.
156|
157|“선배! 속도를 좀 늦춰 주…….”
158|
159|“그건 곤란할 것 같군.”
160|
161|무송이 내 말을 칼같이 잘라 냈다.
162|
163|장강에서 나고 자란 사람답게, 마치 평지에서처럼 우뚝 서 있는 그가 손을 들어 전방을 가리켰다.
164|
165|“보이나?”
166|
167|보이냐니. 뭘 말하는 거지?
168|
169|눈을 가늘게 뜬 나는 그의 손가락이 향하는 곳을 응시했다.
170|
171|공력을 끌어 올려 눈에 집중하자, 비약적으로 상승한 안력(眼力)이 출렁이는 강물에 자욱하게 깔린 안개 너머를 꿰뚫어 본다.
172|
173|‘저건…….’
174|
175|보인다.
176|
177|선박 중에서도 가장 날렵한 축에 들어가는 쾌조선조차 겨우 두 척이 간신히 지나갈 법한 좁은 폭.
178|
179|그리고 그 앞에서 칼날처럼 회오리치는 거센 와류(渦流)가.
180|
181|콰아아아, 콰득!
182|
183|어디서 떠내려온 것인지, 반경만 백여 장에 달하는 와류에 휘말린 커다란 통나무 하나가 수압을 이기지 못하고 부서진다.
184|
185|그렇게 튕겨 나간 통나무의 파편 일부는, 수문장처럼 와류 뒤에 우뚝 선 거대한 바위와 부딪쳐 산산이 조각났다.
186|
187|‘바다도 아니고 강에 저런 소용돌이라니.’
188|
189|신비로우면서도, 한편으로는 등골이 서늘해지는 광경.
190|
191|그리고 지금 쾌조선에 탄 이 자리의 모든 사람은 저 엄청난 와류의 정체를 알고 있었다.
192|
193|“천령폭(天靈瀑)!”
194|
195|누군가가 비명처럼 외친 한마디.
196|
197|맞다. 저것이 바로 천령폭이다.
198|
199|장강수로맹의 동정채를 천혜의 요새로 만들어 준 자연의 산물이자, 오랜 세월 동안 숱한 목숨과 선박을 집어삼킨 괴물.
200|
201|적천강이 당장이라도 질식할 것 같은 얼굴로 선언했다.
202|
203|“배 돌려. 저걸 건널 바에야 정마대전을 한 번 더 치르겠다.”
204|
205|이어 궁기방과 혁무진이 이미 질식한 것 같은 얼굴로 말했다.
206|
207|“무송 선배. 제발 살려 주십시오. 차라리 거지 소굴에서 구걸을 하겠습니다.”
208|
209|“조장님. 그동안 감사했습니다. 저 이제 무림인 그만할게요. 고향 내려가서 비단 팔고 싶어요.”
210|
211|“……비단보다 네 영혼이 먼저 팔린 것 같은데.”
212|
213|이렇게 말하는 나도 겁이 나지 않는 것은 아니다.
214|
215|빠르게 가까워지는 거대한 와류를 보고 있자니, 나 스스로가 개미지옥에 빠진 한 마리 개미가 된 기분이었다.
216|
217|‘시벌, 우선 바위에 맞아서 개박살이 난 다음에 화장실 변기 물 내리는 것처럼 쏙 빨려 들어갈 것 같은데.’
218|
219|대자연이 주는 공포 앞에서는 시스템도, 초절정의 무공도 별 소용없는 것처럼 느껴졌다.
220|
221|만일 누군가 나를 장강 한가운데에 빠트린다면 어떻게든 헤엄쳐 나올 자신이 있지만, 저런 엄청난 소용돌이에 휩쓸린다면…… 그때는 정말이지 끝장이다.
222|
223|“후우, 후.”
224|
225|심호흡하는 내 어깨 위에 두꺼운 손 하나가 올라왔다.
226|
227|“막내야.”
228|
229|제법 장신인 나조차도 고개를 들어 올려다봐야 하는 거한, 진위경이 담담한 표정으로 입을 열었다.
230|
231|“아무것도 걱정하지 말거라.”
232|
233|형님 소리가 절로 나올 수밖에 없는 침착성이다.
234|
235|물을 병적으로 싫어하는 적천강은 둘째 치고 초절정의 경지에 오른 나조차도 간담이 서늘해질 정도인데, 무공으로는 한참 아랫줄인 진위경은 한 치의 흔들림도 없었다. 이래서 큰형이고, 소가주인 거구나.
236|
237|“큰형님…….”
238|
239|“그래.”
240|
241|진위경이 희미하게 웃으며 고개를 끄덕였다.
242|
243|“귀신이 되어서도 우리 형제의 우애는 영원할 것이다.”
244|
245|“예?”
246|
247|“돌아가신 부모님이 눈앞에 어른거리는구나. 천령폭에서 우리를 향해 손짓하고 계시는 듯해.”
248|
249|“……아버지는 아직 살아 계시지 않아요?”
250|
251|“다시 소식이 끊긴 지 오래됐다. 그냥 죽은 셈 치자꾸나.”
252|
253|큰형님은 얼어 죽을. 그냥 큰 새끼다.
254|
255|그 와중에 가문 짬 때리고 도망쳤다고 멀쩡히 살아 있는 아버지까지 죽여 버리는 클라스.
256|
257|‘시펄…….’
258|
259|주위를 둘러보니 이미 대부분 반쯤 정신이 나간 상태로 대자연이 주는 비트에 몸을 맡기는 중이다.
260|
261|나는 마지막 희망을 담아 무송을 바라보았다.
262|
263|“저기, 무송 선배.”
264|
265|“미안하지만, 멈추기에는 늦었네.”
266|
267|콰아아아아! 콰드득!
268|
269|“어, 시발 진짜네.”
270|
271|무송이 굳은 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
272|
273|“꽉 잡게. 나와 수하들 역시 최선을 다할 테니.”
274|

Looking as though he might suffocate at any moment, Jeok Cheongang declared, “Turn the ship around. I would rather fight the Great Faction War all over again than cross that.”

[P100]
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin spoke next, their faces suggesting they had already suffocated.

[P101]
“Senior Mu Song, please save us. I would rather spend my life begging in a beggars’ den.”

[P102]
“Captain, thank you for everything. I’m done with Murim. I want to go home and sell silk.”

[P103]
“…It looks like your soul will be sold before the silk.”

[P104]
Not that I wasn’t scared myself.

[P105]
Watching that enormous whirlpool rush toward us made me feel like an ant tumbling into an antlion’s pit.

[P106]
*Fuck. We’re going to smash against that rock and get blown to pieces, then get sucked straight down like someone flushed a toilet.*

[P107]
Before the terror of nature itself, even the System and Supreme Peak martial arts seemed useless.

[P108]
If someone dropped me into the middle of the Yangtze, I was confident I could somehow swim to shore. But if I got caught in a whirlpool like that…

[P109]
Then I really was finished.

[P110]
“Whew. Whew.”

[P111]
As I took deep breaths, a thick hand settled on my shoulder.

[P112]
“My youngest.”

[P113]
Even as a fairly tall man myself, I had to tilt my head back to look up at the giant beside me. Jin Wikyung spoke with a calm expression.

[P114]
“Do not worry about a thing.”

[P115]
His composure alone made me want to call him Eldest Brother.

[P116]
Jeok Cheongang had a pathological hatred of water, so he was one thing, but even I—a Supreme Peak master—felt my blood run cold. Yet Jin Wikyung, whose martial arts were far beneath ours, showed not the slightest trace of fear.

[P117]
*So this is why he’s my eldest brother. Why he’s the Lesser Family Head.*

[P118]
“Eldest Brother…”

[P119]
“Yes.”

[P120]
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and nodded.

[P121]
“Even as ghosts, the bond between us brothers will endure forever.”

[P122]
“What?”

[P123]
“I can see our departed parents before my eyes. It is as though they are beckoning to us from Tianling Falls.”

[P124]
“…Isn’t Father still alive?”

[P125]
“We lost contact with him again a long time ago. Let us simply consider him dead.”

[P126]
*Eldest brother, my ass. He’s just a big bastard.*

[P127]
Our father had dumped the entire family on him and run away, and Jin Wikyung had just declared the perfectly healthy man dead.

[P128]
*Shit…*

[P129]
I looked around. Most of the people aboard were already half out of their minds, surrendering their bodies to the beat of Mother Nature.

[P130]
With my last shred of hope, I looked at Mu Song.

[P131]
“Senior Mu Song.”

[P132]
“I’m sorry, but it is too late to stop.”

[P133]
Whoooosh! Crack!

[P134]
“Oh, fuck. He’s right.”

[P135]
Mu Song nodded, his expression grim.

[P136]
“Hold on tight. My men and I will do our best.”

[P137]
“What? What do you mean, do your best?”

[P138]
“Do you think every province has its own Tianling Falls? I have only crossed it three or four times, when I came to Hubei to visit Uncle Hwang. We have no choice but to trust in the League’s swift ships and the skills we have honed over the years.”

[P139]
“W-wait. So you’re saying… you’re a Tianling Falls newbie?”

[P140]
“I do not know why you are suddenly bringing up Liu Bei,[^1] but of course I am unfamiliar with it. Ever since leaving headquarters and becoming a Stronghold Lord, I have spent all my time in Sichuan.”

[P141]
He had a point.

[P142]
A fucking punchable point.

[P143]
Half out of my mind, I barely managed to squeeze out the words.

[P144]
“You’ve got to be kidding me. Why are you only telling us something this important now?”

[P145]
“Great Hero Zhuge told me not to tell anyone else.”

[P146]
What?

[P147]
My head snapped around at lightning speed. The disciples of both factions stood rigid with tension, and at their center was one man.

[P148]
Zhuge Feng met my gaze and laughed heartily as the rising spray pelted his face.

[P149]
“A wise man leads his allies, while a strategist deceives even his allies! Now that we have all climbed onto the tiger’s back, let us ride it to the bitter end!”

[P150]
“……!”

[P151]
“……!”

[P152]
Was this really happening?

[P153]
Every last one of us was left speechless.

[P154]
Jeok Cheongang, meanwhile, lost his mind.

[P155]
“That fucking son of a bitch…!”

[P156]
It was one of the most spectacular eruptions of rage I had ever witnessed.

[P157]
But just as Jeok Cheongang rolled his eyes back until only the whites showed and prepared to charge—

[P158]
“Everyone, hold on tight!”

[P159]
At Mu Song’s urgent shout, the whirlpool of Tianling Falls opened its maw wide and slammed into the swift ship.

[P160]
KRA-KOOOOM!

[P161]
[^1]: In Korean, “newbie” is commonly pronounced *nyubi*, which Mu Song mistakes for *Yubi*, the Korean reading of Liu Bei.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Looking as though he might suffocate at any moment, Jeok Cheongang declared, “Turn the ship around. I would rather fight the Great Faction War all over again than cross that.”

[P100]
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin spoke next, their faces suggesting they had already suffocated.

[P101]
“Senior Mu Song, please save us. I would rather spend my life begging in a beggars’ den.”

[P102]
“Captain, thank you for everything. I’m done with Murim. I want to go home and sell silk.”

[P103]
“…It looks like your soul will be sold before the silk.”

[P104]
Not that I wasn’t scared myself.

[P105]
Watching that enormous whirlpool rush toward us made me feel like an ant tumbling into an antlion’s pit.

[P106]
*Fuck. We’re going to smash against that rock and get blown to pieces, then get sucked straight down like someone flushed a toilet.*

[P107]
Before the terror of nature itself, even the System and Supreme Peak martial arts seemed useless.

[P108]
If someone dropped me into the middle of the Yangtze, I was confident I could somehow swim to shore. But if I got caught in a whirlpool like that…

[P109]
Then I really was finished.

[P110]
“Whew. Whew.”

[P111]
As I took deep breaths, a thick hand settled on my shoulder.

[P112]
“My youngest.”

[P113]
Even as a fairly tall man myself, I had to tilt my head back to look up at the giant beside me. Jin Wikyung spoke with a calm expression.

[P114]
“Do not worry about a thing.”

[P115]
His composure alone made me want to call him Eldest Brother.

[P116]
Jeok Cheongang had a pathological hatred of water, so he was one thing, but even I—a Supreme Peak master—felt my blood run cold. Yet Jin Wikyung, whose martial arts were far beneath ours, showed not the slightest trace of fear.

[P117]
*So this is why he’s my eldest brother. Why he’s the Lesser Family Head.*

[P118]
“Eldest Brother…”

[P119]
“Yes.”

[P120]
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and nodded.

[P121]
“Even as ghosts, the bond between us brothers will endure forever.”

[P122]
“What?”

[P123]
“I can see our departed parents before my eyes. It is as though they are beckoning to us from Tianling Falls.”

[P124]
“…Isn’t Father still alive?”

[P125]
“We lost contact with him again a long time ago. Let us simply consider him dead.”

[P126]
*Eldest brother, my ass. He’s just a big bastard.*

[P127]
Our father had dumped the entire family on him and run away, and Jin Wikyung had just declared the perfectly healthy man dead.

[P128]
*Shit…*

[P129]
I looked around. Most of the people aboard were already half out of their minds, surrendering their bodies to the beat of Mother Nature.

[P130]
With my last shred of hope, I looked at Mu Song.

[P131]
“Senior Mu Song.”

[P132]
“I’m sorry, but it is too late to stop.”

[P133]
Whoooosh! Crack!

[P134]
“Oh, fuck. He’s right.”

[P135]
Mu Song nodded, his expression grim.

[P136]
“Hold on tight. My men and I will do our best.”

[P137]
“What? What do you mean, do your best?”

[P138]
“Do you think every province has its own Tianling Falls? I have only crossed it three or four times, when I came to Hubei to visit Uncle Hwang. We have no choice but to trust in the League’s swift ships and the skills we have honed over the years.”

[P139]
“W-wait. So you’re saying… you’re a Tianling Falls newbie?”

[P140]
“I do not know why you are suddenly bringing up Liu Bei,[^1] but of course I am unfamiliar with it. Ever since leaving headquarters and becoming a Stronghold Lord, I have spent all my time in Sichuan.”

[P141]
He had a point.

[P142]
A fucking punchable point.

[P143]
Half out of my mind, I barely managed to squeeze out the words.

[P144]
“You’ve got to be kidding me. Why are you only telling us something this important now?”

[P145]
“Great Hero Zhuge told me not to tell anyone else.”

[P146]
What?

[P147]
My head snapped around at lightning speed. The disciples of both factions stood rigid with tension, and at their center was one man.

[P148]
Zhuge Feng met my gaze and laughed heartily as the rising spray pelted his face.

[P149]
“A wise man leads his allies, while a strategist deceives even his allies! Now that we have all climbed onto the tiger’s back, let us ride it to the bitter end!”

[P150]
“……!”

[P151]
“……!”

[P152]
Was this really happening?

[P153]
Every last one of us was left speechless.

[P154]
Jeok Cheongang, meanwhile, lost his mind.

[P155]
“That fucking son of a bitch…!”

[P156]
It was one of the most spectacular eruptions of rage I had ever witnessed.

[P157]
But just as Jeok Cheongang rolled his eyes back until only the whites showed and prepared to charge—

[P158]
“Everyone, hold on tight!”

[P159]
At Mu Song’s urgent shout, the whirlpool of Tianling Falls opened its maw wide and slammed into the swift ship.

[P160]
KRA-KOOOOM!

[P161]
[^1]: In Korean, “newbie” is commonly pronounced *nyubi*, which Mu Song mistakes for *Yubi*, the Korean reading of Liu Bei.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“You have spent all that time at Wudang’s headquarters, so it is only natural that you would not know. But… may I ask what became of the matter you mentioned last time?”

[P21]
“Our Sect Leader is personally working on it with the disciples of the main sect. In exchange, he sent this old Daoist here, since I was doing nothing but sitting around and consuming grain.”

[P22]
“Doing nothing but consuming grain? With Perfected Being Hyeongong joining us, this junior feels as though he has gained an army of thousands.”

[P23]
Zhuge Feng was not merely being polite. He meant every word.

[P24]
Perfected Being Hyeongong.

[P25]
That was the Daoist name of the old man in the heavily patched robe, with a single worn Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword hanging at his waist.

[P26]
Neither his position within Wudang nor his generational seniority in Murim was inferior to Zhuge Feng’s.

[P27]
If anything, he stood equal to Zhuge Feng—or even above him.

[P28]
Unlike Zhuge Feng, who had yet to turn sixty, Perfected Being Hyeongong was a master of the previous generation who had distinguished himself during the Great Faction War. He was also the current Wudang Sect Leader’s Junior Brother.

[P29]
*And one of the Supreme Peak masters Wudang is so proud of.*

[P30]
Perfected Being Hyeongong was the swordsman said to have reached the ultimate depths of Wudang’s supreme technique, the Taiji Wisdom Sword.

[P31]
Even as Family Head of the Zhuge Clan, Zhuge Feng spoke to him with marked respect in front of everyone. That alone showed the regard he had for Hyeongong.

[P32]
Of course, there was one exception to all this.

[P33]
“That little punk has grown.”

[P34]
At the words of Jeok Cheongang—Murim’s own Bodhidharma-tier old-timer—I muttered in disbelief.

[P35]
“He sure has. He’s grown so much his beard turned white.”

[P36]
“How old was he the last time I saw him? Thirty? Hah. Time certainly flies. Those soft-fuzzed little brats have all become Sect Leaders and Elders.”

[P37]
“Soft fuzz? At thirty, wouldn’t he have had a full bush down there?”

[P38]
Jeok Cheongang glared at me with fire in his eyes.

[P39]
“Judging by the way you keep nitpicking my every word, you must want every hair below your waist plucked out.”

[P40]
“Why would you say something like that?”

[P41]
I had absolutely no desire to receive a Fire King Zilean waxing on the deck of a swift ship.

[P42]
I waved my hands at the speed of light, then stole a sidelong glance at Jeok Cheongang.

[P43]
“Since we’re on the subject, may I ask exactly how venerable your years are?”

[P44]
“Venerable?”

[P45]
Even under normal circumstances, Jeok Cheongang treated being called old as another way of asking him to kill you. I awkwardly tried again.

[P46]
“…Then, your age?”

[P47]
“My age?”

[P48]
Seriously, what more did he want? The man was over a hundred.

[P49]
I asked with all the exasperation I could muster.

[P50]
“Cheongang, how old are you?”

[P51]
Whack!

[P52]
Right. I knew that would happen.

[P53]
Jeok Cheongang smacked the back of my head like a bolt of lightning, then answered in a bored voice.

[P54]
“I stopped counting after one hundred.”

[P55]
“So how long ago was the last time you counted?”

[P56]
“Five thousand years ago. Satisfied?”

[P57]
Cheongpung, who had been dangling from the nearby bow, dropped his jaw.

[P58]
“Wow! Five thousand years old!”

[P59]
“…Does that little punk not know how to doubt anything?”

[P60]
“…That’s just how he is. Anyway, you look unbelievably young for your age.”

[P61]
Jeok Cheongang stared hard at me.

[P62]
“Would you like to know more?”

[P63]
“Of course not.”

[P64]
Honestly, I did want to know, but judging by his expression, this was something I was better off not knowing.

[P65]
He was sensitive about his age at the best of times. Worse, being aboard a swift ship racing over rougher currents and through stronger winds than ever seemed to be causing him tremendous stress.

[P66]
“When the hell is this goddamned piece of wood going to stop?”

[P67]
Right then, as though it had heard his complaint, the goddamned piece of wood sped up even more.

[P68]
Whoooosh!

[P69]
A column of water shot high into the air, and the once-steady hull began rocking from side to side.

[P70]
Cheongpung cheered at the sudden violent motion like a child visiting an amusement park on Children’s Day.

[P71]
Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang, who still had not recovered from their little dip in the Yangtze, let out ear-splitting screams. Mungyeong alone remained perfectly balanced, but when he noticed everyone looking at him, he tactfully grabbed the railing.

[P72]
And Jeok Cheongang…

[P73]
“Uhh! Uhhhhhhhh!”

[P74]
He was panicking so badly that no one would have guessed his title was the Fire King.

[P75]
Good God, look at those bulging eyes. They could put his face across an entire subway car as a Gangnam plastic surgery clinic’s double-eyelid success story.

[P76]
Dodging the water splashing into my face, I shouted at Mu Song.

[P77]
“Senior! Could you slow down a little—”

[P78]
“That will be difficult.”

[P79]
Mu Song cut me off sharply.

[P80]
Like a man born and raised on the Yangtze, he stood tall as though his feet were planted on level ground. He raised one hand and pointed ahead.

[P81]
“Can you see it?”

[P82]
See what?

[P83]
I narrowed my eyes and stared where he was pointing.

[P84]
I drew up my internal energy and focused it into my eyes. My dramatically enhanced vision pierced the dense fog blanketing the churning river.

[P85]
*That’s…*

[P86]
I saw it.

[P87]
A passage so narrow that even swift ships, among the sleekest of all vessels, could barely squeeze through two abreast.

[P88]
And directly before it, a violent whirlpool twisting like a blade.

[P89]
Whoooosh! Crack!

[P90]
A massive log that had drifted in from parts unknown was caught in the whirlpool, which stretched more than a hundred zhang in radius. Unable to withstand the crushing water pressure, it snapped apart.

[P91]
The splintered pieces went flying and struck a gigantic rock looming behind the whirlpool like a gatekeeper, shattering into fragments.

[P92]
*A whirlpool like that in a river? Not the sea, but a river?*

[P93]
The sight was as wondrous as it was chilling.

[P94]
And everyone aboard the swift ships knew the identity of that monstrous whirlpool.

[P95]
“Tianling Falls!”

[P96]
Someone screamed the name.

[P97]
That was right. This was Tianling Falls.

[P98]
It was the natural barrier that had made the Yangtze River Channel League’s Donghu Stronghold an impregnable fortress—and a monster that had swallowed countless lives and ships over the long years.

[P99]
Looking as though he might suffocate at any moment, Jeok Cheongang declared, “Turn the ship around. I would rather fight the Great Faction War all over again than cross that.”

[P100]
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin spoke next, their faces suggesting they had already suffocated.

[P101]
“Senior Mu Song, please save us. I would rather spend my life begging in a beggars’ den.”

[P102]
“Captain, thank you for everything. I’m done with Murim. I want to go home and sell silk.”

[P103]
“…It looks like your soul will be sold before the silk.”

[P104]
Not that I wasn’t scared myself.

[P105]
Watching that enormous whirlpool rush toward us made me feel like an ant tumbling into an antlion’s pit.

[P106]
*Fuck. We’re going to smash against that rock and get blown to pieces, then get sucked straight down like someone flushed a toilet.*

[P107]
Before the terror of nature itself, even the System and Supreme Peak martial arts seemed useless.

[P108]
If someone dropped me into the middle of the Yangtze, I was confident I could somehow swim to shore. But if I got caught in a whirlpool like that…

[P109]
Then I really was finished.

[P110]
“Whew. Whew.”

[P111]
As I took deep breaths, a thick hand settled on my shoulder.

[P112]
“My youngest.”

[P113]
Even as a fairly tall man myself, I had to tilt my head back to look up at the giant beside me. Jin Wikyung spoke with a calm expression.

[P114]
“Do not worry about a thing.”

[P115]
His composure alone made me want to call him Eldest Brother.

[P116]
Jeok Cheongang had a pathological hatred of water, so he was one thing, but even I—a Supreme Peak master—felt my blood run cold. Yet Jin Wikyung, whose martial arts were far beneath ours, showed not the slightest trace of fear.

[P117]
*So this is why he’s my eldest brother. Why he’s the Lesser Family Head.*

[P118]
“Eldest Brother…”

[P119]
“Yes.”

[P120]
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and nodded.

[P121]
“Even as ghosts, the bond between us brothers will endure forever.”

[P122]
“What?”

[P123]
“I can see our departed parents before my eyes. It is as though they are beckoning to us from Tianling Falls.”

[P124]
“…Isn’t Father still alive?”

[P125]
“We lost contact with him again a long time ago. Let us simply consider him dead.”

[P126]
*Eldest brother, my ass. He’s just a big bastard.*

[P127]
Our father had dumped the entire family on him and run away, and Jin Wikyung had just declared the perfectly healthy man dead.

[P128]
*Shit…*

[P129]
I looked around. Most of the people aboard were already half out of their minds, surrendering their bodies to the beat of Mother Nature.

[P130]
With my last shred of hope, I looked at Mu Song.

[P131]
“Senior Mu Song.”

[P132]
“I’m sorry, but it is too late to stop.”

[P133]
Whoooosh! Crack!

[P134]
“Oh, fuck. He’s right.”

[P135]
Mu Song nodded, his expression grim.

[P136]
“Hold on tight. My men and I will do our best.”

[P137]
“What? What do you mean, do your best?”

[P138]
“Do you think every province has its own Tianling Falls? I have only crossed it three or four times, when I came to Hubei to visit Uncle Hwang. We have no choice but to trust in the League’s swift ships and the skills we have honed over the years.”

[P139]
“W-wait. So you’re saying… you’re a Tianling Falls newbie?”

[P140]
“I do not know why you are suddenly bringing up Liu Bei,[^1] but of course I am unfamiliar with it. Ever since leaving headquarters and becoming a Stronghold Lord, I have spent all my time in Sichuan.”

[P141]
He had a point.

[P142]
A fucking punchable point.

[P143]
Half out of my mind, I barely managed to squeeze out the words.

[P144]
“You’ve got to be kidding me. Why are you only telling us something this important now?”

[P145]
“Great Hero Zhuge told me not to tell anyone else.”

[P146]
What?

[P147]
My head snapped around at lightning speed. The disciples of both factions stood rigid with tension, and at their center was one man.

[P148]
Zhuge Feng met my gaze and laughed heartily as the rising spray pelted his face.

[P149]
“A wise man leads his allies, while a strategist deceives even his allies! Now that we have all climbed onto the tiger’s back, let us ride it to the bitter end!”

[P150]
“……!”

[P151]
“……!”

[P152]
Was this really happening?

[P153]
Every last one of us was left speechless.

[P154]
Jeok Cheongang, meanwhile, lost his mind.

[P155]
“That fucking son of a bitch…!”

[P156]
It was one of the most spectacular eruptions of rage I had ever witnessed.

[P157]
But just as Jeok Cheongang rolled his eyes back until only the whites showed and prepared to charge—

[P158]
“Everyone, hold on tight!”

[P159]
At Mu Song’s urgent shout, the whirlpool of Tianling Falls opened its maw wide and slammed into the swift ship.

[P160]
KRA-KOOOOM!

[P161]
[^1]: In Korean, “newbie” is commonly pronounced *nyubi*, which Mu Song mistakes for *Yubi*, the Korean reading of Liu Bei.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.

- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
